conjecture: An integer $m \geq 0$ is a sum of two triangular numbers $m = T_a + T_b$ (where $T_k = \frac{k(k+1)}{2}$ and $a, b \geq 0$) if and only if $4m+1$ is a sum of two squares.
For every positive integer $n$, $10^{10^{10^n}} + 10^{10^n} + 10^n - 1$ is not prime (i.e., it is always composite).
Does $4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z$ have a positive integer solution in $x, y, z$, for every prime $p$?

Carmichael's totient function conjecture: For every positive integer $n$, there exists another positive integer $m \neq n$ such that $\varphi(m) = \varphi(n)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. In other words, no value of the totient function is achieved exactly once.
Erdos-Straus: Does $4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z$ have a positive integer solution for every integer $n\ge 2$

Holroyd-Talbot Conjecture (2005): For any graph G, if $1 \leq r \leq \mu(G)/2$, then $G$ is $r$-EKR (there exists a vertex $v$ such that the star $I^r_v(G)$ is a maximum intersecting family of independent $r$-sets), and strictly $r$-EKR (every maximum intersecting family is a star) when $1 < r < \mu(G)/2$. Here $\mu(G) denotes the size of the smallest maximal independent set of G (equivalently, the smallest independent dominating set).
